description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till organisationen PEN International om totalt 36 MSEK under en fyraårsperiod 2020-2023. För denna period har PEN utvecklat en strategi, med fokus på fyra tematiska områden:
1) Skapa nya utrymmen för litteratur, språk, debatt, dialog, idéer och åsikter. 2) Förbättra situationen för utsatta skribenter på flykt, som är fängslade eller på annat sätt förföljda. 3) Påverka strukturella hot och barriärer mot yttrandefrihet. 4) Stärka den institutionella kapaciteten och hållbarheten hos PEN som organisation.
Total budget för perioden är cirka 94 MSEK. Sidas stöd uppgår till 36 MSEK.

PEN International is a global network consisting of more than 20 000 writers, affiliated with over 150 federated centres in more than 100 countries. The overall goal of the organisation is to promote and defend freedom of expression, literatures, linguistic diversity and mutual respect and tolerace across borders.
PEN:s strategic plan for 2020-2023 has four thematic domains: 1) Creating new spaces for literature, language, debate, dialogue ideas and opinions. 2) Improving the situation of writers at risk who are displaced, imprisoned or otherwise persecuted. 3) Addressing structural threats and barriers to freedom of expression. 4) Strengthening the institutional capacity and sustainability of PEN, so that the movement is fully representative and relevant.
The total budget for the four-year period is around 94 MSEK. Sidas contribution for this period amounts to 36 MSEK.

PEN International has adopted a new strategy for the years 2024-2028. The intended global outcomes are slightly changed with a clearer focus on human rights and advocacy. The document is also shorter. Sida assesses that the new strategy has an even stronger foundation in HRBA than the previous one. The outcomes are:
Outcome 1: Creating spaces for literature, language, debates, dialogue, ideas and opinions.
Outcome 2: Strengthening human rights policy and practice.
Outcome 3: Improvement in the situation of writers at risk who are imprisoned or otherwise persecuted.
Outcome 4: Strengthen the institutional capacity, standing and sustainability of PEN Centres, so that the movement is an effective champion of free expression for all.

description.narrative:
During the last year of the agreement, 2024, PEN reports the following, among other results:
- PEN has continued its work to monitor crimes and threats against writers and persecution and imprisonment of writers with its Case list 2024, where 138 attacks have been documented. The report shows an alarming trend where censorship, imprisonment and threats against writers are increasing, due to the writers' gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation or religious beliefs.
- PEN has drawn attention, for example, to the situation of journalists in North and South America through the Day of the Dead campaign. PEN has also drawn attention to members who have been killed by Russia's aggression in Ukraine.
- PEN works with campaigns and advocacy to persuade regimes to release imprisoned writers, journalists and artists. In 2024, several such campaigns were successful, for example in Nigeria, Gambia, Honduras, Canada. Cuba, El Salvador, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Serbia, Montenegro, Turkey, Morocco and India. Writers have also been released from prison after campaigns in regimes such as Russia, Belarus and Iran.
- 85 grants from PEN's Emergency Fund have been awarded to writers in acute crisis and danger. Several of the writers who have received support are LGBTQI people, who are persecuted because of this affiliation.
In 2024, PEN International has continued its normative work at a global level with advocacy work within the UN system and in the EU institutions. PEN has written and adopted several declarations and written several reports, including "Toxic Narratives" on the situation of journalists in the Western Balkans. The report received attention within the EU and has led to cooperation and focus on improving the situation of press freedom in the EU candidate countries.
Through its Civil Society Programme, PEN local clubs have worked to disseminate literature, language and cultural rights. PEN clubs have commissioned articles from authors writing in minority languages in both Latin America and Africa. The articles have been published in the press and published as anthologies. The project around the Moomin saga "The Invisible Child" has continued at the grassroots level and with great effort from volunteers from PEN clubs in Malawi, Togo and South Africa (via PEN Afrikaans).
In Ukraine, PEN Ukraine, with the support of PEN International, has worked under difficult circumstances to strengthen dialogue and conversation within civil society and to give people access to Ukrainian and international literature. PEN Ukraine has arranged 28 events in the Dialogues on War series, and organized four trips to the front to spread knowledge and insight into how culture is affected by war.
Right now, as far as Sida can assess, PEN International is the only civil society organisation which works on a global mandate with protection of writers, poets and artists, and one of few that works with advocacy within the UN system on the issue of Artistic freedom and the rights of artists. There are other organisations that works regionally and locally with the same issues, but there is a need for a strong global organisation to gather the voices, and here PEN plays an important role.
